_readme: Single source for the en/ site root (nav, SEO, catalog, sitemap). Human-readable fields are translation units tracked in i18n/ledger.json. Rebuild with: SITE_ROOT=en node scripts/build_nav.js

site.title: Home Assistant Tailscale Remote Access Guide
site.subtitle: Safe way home, no open ports
site.description: 12-chapter Home Assistant Tailscale app guide: install, join the tailnet, private remote access, least privilege, subnet router basics, troubleshooting and maintenance.
site.footerMeta: Screenshots are from the official Home Assistant interface. Home Assistant is a trademark of the Open Home Foundation; this site is not affiliated with it.

hub._readme: index.html is the hand-maintained Resource Hub for the four resource types; build_nav does not touch it. The tutorial catalog page is generated by build_nav into the file named by catalog. pages are standalone single-file handbooks under the hub (each with its own head and styles); they go into the sitemap and the check_links allowlist but are not subject to the content-page rules.

chapters.navLabel: Inventory and security boundaries before you start
chapters.title: Before you start
chapters.pagerTitle: 01 · Inventory and security boundaries before you start
chapters.card: Start by deciding who may reach your Home Assistant, which devices join the tailnet, and what this guide deliberately leaves out.
chapters.description: Planning remote access with Tailscale and Home Assistant: tailnet, devices, least privilege, security boundaries and pre-flight inventory.

chapters.title: Install the app
chapters.card: Find Tailscale on the Home Assistant Apps page, install it and start it; do not guess at settings, and do not rush to make the service public.
chapters.description: Home Assistant Tailscale app install guide: the Apps page, install, start, the Web UI and the first round of security checks.

chapters.navLabel: Log in and join your tailnet
chapters.title: Join the tailnet
chapters.pagerTitle: 03 · Log in and join your tailnet
chapters.card: Use the Tailscale app's Web UI to make this Home Assistant a member of your tailnet, then confirm that it appears in the admin console.
chapters.description: Home Assistant Tailscale app login and joining the tailnet: Web UI sign-in, the Machines list, device names and connection checks.

chapters.navLabel: Read the app's status and logs
chapters.title: Status and logs
chapters.pagerTitle: 04 · Read the app's status and logs
chapters.card: Before you change any network option, learn to read the app's status and logs; that is the shortest path when troubleshooting.
chapters.description: Home Assistant Tailscale app status and logs: startup, connection checks, safe settings and how to read common errors.

chapters.navLabel: Open Home Assistant safely from the tailnet
chapters.title: Open HA remotely
chapters.pagerTitle: 05 · Open Home Assistant safely from the tailnet
chapters.card: Let only phones and computers that have joined the tailnet open HA, and set up a verifiable, private remote-access workflow first.
chapters.description: Private remote access to Home Assistant over Tailscale: phones, laptops, tailnet devices and a safe test procedure.

chapters.navLabel: Machines, names and the device lifecycle
chapters.title: Manage devices
chapters.pagerTitle: 06 · Machines, names and the device lifecycle
chapters.card: Treat Home Assistant, your phone and your laptop as Machines you manage: name them, audit them, deauthorize the devices you no longer use, and check key expiry.
chapters.description: Managing Tailscale Machines: naming Home Assistant devices, device inventory, key expiry and safe handling when someone leaves or swaps hardware.

chapters.navLabel: Least privilege: who can reach what
chapters.title: Least privilege
chapters.pagerTitle: 07 · Least privilege: who can reach what
chapters.card: Tailscale is not a reason to assume "install it and everything can reach everything". Check the policy in the admin console first, then write the access scope to be exactly what is needed.
chapters.description: Least privilege with Tailscale access controls: tailnet policy, grants, ACL, users, tags and Home Assistant access boundaries.

chapters.navLabel: Choose Serve: an HTTPS entry point inside the tailnet
chapters.title: Serve
chapters.pagerTitle: 08 · Choose Serve: an HTTPS entry point inside the tailnet
chapters.card: When you need a clean HTTPS entry point, first understand the security difference between Serve and Funnel; this guide covers tailnet-only Serve and nothing else.
chapters.description: Home Assistant Tailscale Serve: tailnet-only HTTPS, share_homeassistant, trusted_proxies and where the Funnel risk boundary sits.

chapters.navLabel: Subnet router basics: let the tailnet see your home LAN
chapters.title: Subnet router
chapters.pagerTitle: 09 · Subnet router basics: let the tailnet see your home LAN
chapters.card: Let this HA host advertise one subnet of your home LAN only when you are sure you need it; this chapter covers only basic one-way access to a single subnet.
chapters.description: Home Assistant Tailscale subnet router basics: advertise_routes, local_subnets, LAN CIDR, SNAT and route scope.

chapters.navLabel: Approve the subnet route and test end to end
chapters.title: Approve routes
chapters.pagerTitle: 10 · Approve the subnet route and test end to end
chapters.card: An advertised route is not a usable route yet: approve it in Machines, then verify from another tailnet device.
chapters.description: Approving and testing a Tailscale subnet route: Machines, Edit route settings, the Subnets badge and reaching a LAN device.

chapters.navLabel: Daily-use rules for phones and laptops
chapters.title: Daily use
chapters.pagerTitle: 11 · Daily-use rules for phones and laptops
chapters.card: Turn remote use into a repeatable habit: confirm Tailscale first, then open HA, and know where to check when the connection drops.
chapters.description: Daily use of Home Assistant with Tailscale: phones, laptops, tailnet connections, remote access, offline troubleshooting and safe habits.

chapters.navLabel: Troubleshooting, updates and the handover checklist
chapters.title: Troubleshooting and maintenance
chapters.pagerTitle: 12 · Troubleshooting, updates and the handover checklist
chapters.card: Work through one outside-in checklist to handle connection failures, routes you cannot see, expired logins and problems that appear after a settings change.
chapters.description: Home Assistant Tailscale troubleshooting and maintenance: app logs, Machines, route approval, key expiry, updates and the handover checklist.
